newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban militia capture Kabul, no resistance seen.
newsitem.headline: Taleban militia capture Kabul, no resistance seen.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia entered Kabul in tanks and on foot overnight on Friday, meeting little resistance from forces loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani, witnesses said.
There was no fighting in Kabul.

Celebratory bursts of machine-gun fire and occasional explosions echoed across the city at dawn but the Afghan capital was relatively calm as Taleban fighters set up checkpoints to search vehicles, the eyewitnesses said.
All key government installations appeared to be in Taleban hands including the Presidential Palace and the Ministries of Defence, Security and Foreign Affairs.
No government forces were visible on the city's streets.
Civilians were walking in the streets in the morning past Taleban fighters who were controlling crossroads.
Taleban forces entered the city from the east at about 1 a.m. local time (2130 GMT).
They stopped in one street in the diplomatic Wazir Akbar Kahan Li neighbourhood and set up a loudspeaker and recited from the Koran for 15 minutes.
The fate of Rabbani, his military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, and Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar was not immediately known.
A few hours before the taleban arrived, govt troops began pulling out.

Witnesses said tanks, artillery and trucks loaded with soldiers headed north out of the city apparently towards Jabal us-Sharaj, Masood's headquarters at the entrance to the Panjshir valley, where he and his best fighters come from.

Overnight on Thursday Taleban sources in Pakistan had said the Islamic militia appeared poised to capture the capital after seizing the main government airbase north of Kabul and parts of the city, including its abandoned Khwaja Rawash airport.

Deputy foreign minister Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai told Reuters Television at the United Nations late on Thursday that government troops were leaving Kabul to avoid a "bloodbath" with the rebels, and the country's besieged president was considering handing over power.
The minister said Masood had gone north of the city, taking with him jet fighters and other military hardware.
